note: Worked examples. These groups are excluded from every queue, group count, member count, time total and accuracy figure.

examples.title: BGL worked example
examples.summary: Template <*> L3 <*> error(s) (dcr <*> detected and corrected — component KERNEL, level INFO.
examples.sample: … RAS KERNEL INFO 1 L3 EDRAM error(s) (dcr 0x0157) detected and corrected
steps: Open the Messages tab. There are about 100 distinct raw messages in this group.

Open the Fields tab. Field 1 is a count (1, 2, 3 …) and field 3 is a register address such as 0x0157). Both are only identifiers: tick “Instance info” for each. The messages then collapse into just two kinds: EDRAM and directory.
Click a few messages of each kind to read their raw lines, then open the context of one line.
examples.explanation: The level is INFO, not FATAL or FAILURE, and the message says the error was “detected and corrected” — a routine counter report. All BGL alerts come from FATAL / FAILURE levels, so an INFO line is normal even when it contains the word “error”.

examples.title: Thunderbird worked example
examples.sample: acpid: acpid startup succeeded  /  acpid: acpid shutdown succeeded
steps: Open the Fields tab. Field 2 takes the values startup / shutdown. It is a key field (not instance info), so look at both values.
Click each of the two messages to read their raw lines.
Open the context of a line: it sits in a run of service start / stop records written while a node boots or shuts down.
examples.explanation: No published alert rule matches. By definition this is the successful result of a routine operation.

examples.title: HDFS worked example
examples.summary: Count vector: allocate T22×1; write three replicas T5, T9, T11, T26 ×3 each; read T3×1 and T4 (Got exception while serving) ×2; verify T2×3; delete T23, T21 ×3 each.
steps: Open the full log of 2–3 blocks and compare two of them. Their event orders differ (dozens of different orders), but every one is a complete lifecycle: write 3 replicas → read and verify → delete 3 replicas.
Note that “Got exception while serving” appears in the read phase — it is part of the read events.
examples.explanation: The blocks contain only write, read/verify and delete events; the replica count is consistent (3 each) and deletion is complete. A different event order does not change the conclusion.
